response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(fillcount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark HAVING AVG(fillcount) IS NOT NULL), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM per_order), k1 AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.a, p.a - b1.m AS e1 FROM per_order p CROSS JOIN b1 WHERE p.a > b1.m), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS m FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.a, k1.e1, k1.a - b2.m AS e2 FROM k1 CROSS JOIN b2 WHERE k1.a > b2.m) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_fill_quantity, AVG(e1) AS avg_first_excess, AVG(e2) AS avg_second_excess FROM k2

assumptions.assumption: Executions with NULL ordersmark form a single group, which is treated like one order. This follows from the request and from GROUP BY semantics.
Groups whose fillcount values are all NULL have no average, so they are left out of the benchmark and the comparisons.
The second excess is each kept order's average minus the second benchmark, which is the mean of the first-round kept orders' averages. Comparisons are strict (>).
